reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Well if you thought poor “Clarence” was a bit hopeless in “It’s a Wonderful Life” (1946) then wait til you meet “Gabriel” (Keanu Reeves). He’s an entry-level angel, replete with stunted wings, who is charged with stopping careless drovers from texting whilst crashing. He’s bored, and so when he spots the down-at-heel “Ari” (Aziz Ansari) he believes he might have discovered a pet project for himself. This man works in one of those rent-a-person jobs running errands for folks and living on their meagre tips. One such trip sees him at the luxurious home of “Jeff” (Seth Rogan). He’s supposed to clean out his garage, but proves a bit more invaluable than that and is soon hired as his personal factotum. He even gets a company Amex card! That proves very handy when he takes his date “Rosa” (Bianca Araceli) to a restaurant recommended by his new boss and finds the bill pretty eye-watering. Of course, “Jeff” isn’t impressed, promptly fires the man and this is where our angelic intervention goes a bit wonky. “Jeff” and “Ari” swap roles. The former now finds himself homeless and broke, the latter comfortably off in his hilltop palace and poor old “Gabriel” suitably de-winged by his furious boss “Martha” (Sandra Oh) who declares that he will only get them back when he has sorted out his mischief. To do that he needs both men to consent to the swap, but what chance? Especially as an angel with no wings or powers he is not much use when it comes to putting food in their mouths and “Ari” is now all too readily settled in his cashmere and champagne luxury. If you saw the recent “Freaky Friday” remake then this follows similar lines with loads of daft antics combining a good dose of venality with an element of doing the right thing quite amiably. Rogan and Ansari both deliver entertainingly but it’s really Reeves who steals the show as his dejection grows, he turns to all-night dishwashing, chain smoking and begins to realise that there is a lot more to the human being lark than he’d anticipated. There’s nothing especially innovative from the writing or the production, really, it is just a fun stroll that pokes some fun at the fabulously wealthy (who don’t really do anything for their buck) and the struggling family man who works flat out but still has to sleep in his car (until it is towed). Good fun.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content:
Late-stage capitalism... yay
From a technical standpoint this movie has it. It has great visuals, lovely cast, great sound, good music.

But that's not why you watch movies, at least not solely. You watch them to feel something. And this movie only makes you feel even more bereft of space and validity in this late-stage capitalism hellscape we live in. It isn't uplifting. It isn't enlightening. It is not even funny half the time. It just points out how bleak the world is, and I knew that already.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: A well-meaning but overzealous guardian angel causes chaotic fallout when he swaps the lives of a struggling Los Angeles gig worker and a cluelessly wealthy tech investor to prove that money cannot buy happiness.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Gabriel, a low-ranking guardian angel tasked with preventing distracted driving accidents, decides to take on a bigger challenge by intervening in the life of Arj, a desperate Los Angeles gig worker living out of his car. Believing he can prove that wealth does not fix life's problems, Gabriel swaps Arj's life with that of Jeff, a cluelessly rich venture capitalist who recently fired Arj. When Arj thrives in luxury and refuses to give it up, Gabriel loses his celestial status and wings, leaving all three men to navigate the realities of class, money, and purpose.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Arj is a struggling documentary maker stuck working odd tasks through gig-economy apps, sleeping in his car, and picking up shifts at a local hardware store alongside his politically minded love interest, Elena. After a briefly promising job as an assistant to Jeff, a lavish and clueless tech bro, ends with Arj getting fired and his car towed, he hits absolute rock bottom. Observing his plight, Gabriel, an ambitious low-level guardian angel whose usual job is preventing texting-and-driving crashes, decides to intervene to save Arj's soul. Gabriel attempts to teach Arj that wealth is not the answer by executing a life swap between Arj and Jeff, expecting Arj to quickly realize that money cannot buy true fulfillment. However, Gabriel's plan backfires completely when Arj discovers that wealth solves almost all of his immediate problems and happily embraces his new life of comfort. Angry at his unauthorized intervention, Gabriel's heavenly supervisor strips him of his wings and turns him into a mortal, forcing him to experience the grueling realities of human survival firsthand. With Jeff forced to survive on gig work and sleep in a vehicle, and Gabriel struggling as a human, the three must navigate the messy fallouts of status, systemic inequality, and social disconnect. Ultimately, Gabriel and Jeff learn profound lessons about systemic exploitation, while Arj must find the inner motivation to embrace his real life with authentic hope rather than monetary dependence.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Good Fortune centers on Arj, an overworked, underpaid worker in Los Angeles trying to survive by taking odd jobs off an app while living out of his vehicle. After getting fired from a brief trial assisting a wealthy venture capitalist named Jeff, Arj reaches a breaking point. Enter Gabriel, an overeager guardian angel assigned to routine tasks like preventing texting-and-driving accidents, who longs to perform meaningful heavenly deeds. Seeking to give Arj perspective and prove that excessive wealth does not lead to happiness, Gabriel executes a life swap between the poor gig worker and the extravagant capitalist. The magical lesson quickly goes off the rails when Arj finds life as a millionaire vastly superior to his former struggles and resists switching back. Stripped of his powers and wings as punishment by his divine superior, Gabriel is thrust into mortality alongside Jeff, who must now learn how to survive in the precarious gig economy he helped create. Together, the trio navigates the absurdity, comedy, and reality of class divides and social expectations in modern-day Los Angeles.

story_structure.climax: As the chaos escalates and heavenly supervisor oversight threatens to collapse their realities, all three individuals are forced to confront the harsh truths of economic inequality and human connection.
story_structure.conflict: Gabriel, a well-meaning but inept guardian angel, attempts to prove to the struggling worker that money cannot buy happiness by intervening in his life.
story_structure.resolution: Through shared perspective and newfound empathy, each character gains a deeper understanding of what truly brings purpose and fulfillment to life beyond wealth or divine authority.
story_structure.introduction: In Los Angeles, a hardworking gig worker struggles to survive on odd jobs while living out of his car, contrasting sharply with the opulent lifestyle of a carefree, wealthy venture capitalist.
story_structure.risingAction: Gabriel swaps the lives and economic statuses of the gig worker and the venture capitalist, but the plan backfires when the former gig worker happily embraces his new wealth and refuses to go back, forcing Gabriel to lose his wings and experience human life firsthand.
